findings.note: The constraint a₂ = 7a₁ is the key relation of this problem and is neither stated in the served question nor derived anywhere in the solution; a student reading this item alone cannot check where the factor 7 comes from.
findings.fix: Derive the constraint from the three strings first: S₁ over the fixed pulley gives a(P₂) = a₁ (opposite senses); S₂ over P₂ gives a(P₃) = 2a(P₂) + a₁ = 3a₁; S₃ over P₃ gives a₂ = 2a(P₃) + a₁ = 7a₁. Then apply Newton's second law to block 1 (pulled up by 7T) and block 2 (pulled up by T).

question_defect: The served text says 'the same three-pulley chain as before' and the solution leans on a constraint 'found earlier'; the item is served standalone, so the reference points at nothing the student can see. The figure description does supply the tensions T, 2T, 4T but not the acceleration constraint.
notes: Independently derived a₂ = 7a₁ from the three string lengths, then 7T − 10 = a and 20 − T = 14a give 99a = 130; every printed line follows and the numbers match to the last digit. The mistake entry's plain-Atwood value (2−1)·10/3 = 3.33 m/s² is computed correctly.
